overview_text: The BA in Applied Psychology provides students with an understanding of the biological, behavioral, emotional, and cognitive factors influencing human health and well-being. Students develop writing and communications skills and apply research methods and analytic techniques to advance their own research. The program is a series of courses centered on developing students' understanding of the determinants of health, theories and practices related to ameliorating mental health problems, and promoting health and wellness. Each student is required to complete a core course sequence including courses in biology, health sciences, and applied psychology. Core courses include research methods in preparation for a final problem-based capstone project that addresses a community health issue and its relationship to a student's chosen area of specialization in applied psychology. Academic Policies and Procedures Please visit Bouvé College of Health Sciences Undergraduate page for academic policies and procedures, including Academic Appeals . Please visit Bouvé College Learning Outcomes for the specific student learning outcomes for this program.
